cards.subject: Late at night on Holy Thursday, after the Mass of the Lord's Supper, in a large dark stone church. At the left, a side chapel glows as the place of repose: on an altar dressed in white stands a small closed gilded tabernacle, surrounded by many lit candles and white flowers, and a few faithful kneel before it in silent watch, half-length and seen from behind: an old man with his head bowed, a young woman in a white veil, a boy with joined hands. At the right, in shadow, the high altar STRIPPED BARE: plain stone, no cloth, no candles, no flowers; the large cross above it covered with a plain violet veil. Pale moonlight through the tall windows. Hushed, sorrowful, adoring. Keep everything inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin white ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and white; no halo
cards.basis: The end of the Mass of the Lord's Supper as its rubrics in the repo give it (lords-supper.json nos. 38–43): the Blessed Sacrament carried to a place of repose 'suitably decorated' and shut in its tabernacle, the altar stripped, crosses removed or veiled, and the faithful invited to continue adoration during the night. White, the colour of the Lord's Supper that opens the Triduum; the Good Friday veil is violet (good-friday.json no. 15).

cards.subject: A Sunday Mass in Easter Time during the rite of sprinkling with blessed water, in a bright church decked with white lilies. The priest, in a WHITE chasuble with gold orphreys over a white alb, walks slowly down the central aisle, small and seen in profile, sprinkling the people with an aspergillum; a server in cassock and surplice walks beside him carrying the holy-water vessel. The faithful stand in the pews on either side, half-length and seen from behind or in profile, bowing their heads as the drops fall: families, an old man, a girl in a white dress. Behind, in the sanctuary, the tall PASCHAL CANDLE burns on its stand beside the ambo, marked with a simple red cross; the altar in white and gold with its candles lit and white lilies around it. Clear spring morning light fills the church. Joyful, fresh, radiant. Keep everything inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin white ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and white; no halo
cards.basis: The blessing and sprinkling of water, which the Order of Mass puts 'on Sundays, especially in Easter Time' in place of the Penitential Act, the priest 'moving through the church' (order-of-mass.json, order.sprinkling-rite); the paschal candle stands by the ambo and is lit at the more solemn celebrations of the season (easter-vigil.json nos. 17, 70); white for Easter Time (GIRM 346a). Easter Sunday itself has its own card (`easter`), so the formulary is the Second Sunday.

cards.subject: A weekday morning Mass in Easter Time in a small church beside a garden. The priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a WHITE chasuble with gold orphreys over a white alb, his arms extended in prayer; one server in cassock and surplice kneels at the step. The altar has a white frontal with gold embroidery, a crucifix and two lit candles, and a vase of white lilies and spring blossom beside it. Through a tall open window at the side, a sunlit garden: an apple tree in white blossom, fresh green grass, swallows in a clear sky. A few faithful kneel half-length in the foreground, seen from behind or in profile: a gardener holding his straw hat, a young mother with a small girl clutching a yellow daffodil, an elderly man with a cane. Fresh, luminous, peaceful. Keep everyone inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin white ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and white; no halo
cards.basis: The weekday Mass of Easter Time in white (GIRM 346a), with the flowers the season allows; its spring garden stands for new life, after the entrance antiphon of the chosen formulary ('death will no longer have dominion over him'). The paschal candle is left to the Sunday card: the Missal asks it lit at the season's more solemn celebrations.

cards.subject: A Sunday Mass in high summer in a full parish church. The priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a GREEN chasuble over a white alb, raising his hands in prayer, with a deacon in a green dalmatic and two servers in cassock and surplice on the steps. The altar has a white cloth, a crucifix and six tall lit candles, with green leaves and white summer flowers arranged around it, not on it. The tall side windows stand open: through them, fields of ripening golden-green wheat under a deep blue sky with white clouds. In the foreground, half-length and seen from behind, a full congregation stands in the wooden pews in light summer clothes: families, a grandmother, a boy in short trousers, a girl holding a straw hat. Warm, bright, festive but ordinary. Keep everything inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin green ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and green; no halo
cards.basis: Green for Ordinary Time (GIRM 346c) and moderate flowers around the altar (GIRM 305): the full parish at Sunday Mass in summer, where the Ordinary Time I card shows the parish arriving in spring. The Seventeenth Sunday is chosen as the formulary because it always falls after Pentecost and after Trinity Sunday and Corpus Christi (between 24 and 30 July); its antiphon speaks of God gathering his people in his house.

cards.subject: A weekday morning Mass of the Advent Ember Days in the traditional Latin rite, in a stone village church on a grey December morning. The priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, small, in a VIOLET Roman chasuble over a white alb, a violet maniple on his left arm, his hands joined; one server in black cassock and white surplice kneels on the lowest step. The altar has a violet frontal, a crucifix and two lit candles, and no flowers. Beside the altar, a tall clear window looks out on snow-covered fields, a frozen stream and bare trees under low grey clouds, with a soft fall of snow. In the foreground, half-length and seen from behind, a few faithful kneel in the pews: a farmer and his wife in a dark shawl, an old woman in a black lace veil, a young man in a heavy coat. Sober, still, recollected. Keep everyone inside the arched window.
cards.frame: a thin violet ruled line just inside the gold border; the inner window is ROUND-ARCHED like a church window, edged in gold and violet; no halo
cards.basis: The Ember Days are days of fast kept 'to consecrate every season of the year by penance' and to pray for the fruits of the earth (Catechism of St. Pius X, part III, ch. IV, q. 23, in the repo); violet in the traditional missal (Divinum Officium's liturgical_color; Morrow, lesson 138). The winter fields at rest and the snow falling answer the Introit of Ember Wednesday, 'Drop down dew, you heavens'.

cards.subject: Early morning in the first week of Lent at the edge of a village. In the foreground, a farmer in a linen smock sows seed by hand from a sack slung at his side across a freshly ploughed brown field, small and seen in profile, pausing with his cap in his other hand as the church bell rings. Behind him, the little stone church with its doors open: deep inside, small, the priest stands at the altar facing it, AD ORIENTEM, seen from behind, in a VIOLET chasuble with a violet maniple, two candles lit on an altar without flowers; two women in dark veils climb the steps to go in. The Universal Norms (nos. 45–47) keep the same intention for the Ember Days in the new calendar, with a Mass for Various Needs such as 'At Seedtime'.

cards.subject: A morning Mass of the September Ember Days in the traditional Latin rite, in a village church at harvest time. cards.subject: The Entrance at a Sunday Mass, seen from the back of the nave of a tall stone church. Up the central aisle toward the altar moves the procession, everyone small and seen from behind: first a server swinging a smoking thurible; then a server carrying a processional crucifix between two servers with tall lit candles; then two more servers in cassock and surplice; then a reader in a white alb carrying the red-and-gold Book of the Gospels slightly raised before him; last, the priest in a white-and-gold chasuble over a white alb, his hands joined. The congregation stands in the wooden pews on either side, half-length, turned toward the altar. Ahead, at the top of the steps, the altar with a white cloth, a crucifix and lit candles; a soft haze of incense drifts through the light from the high windows. Stately and joyful. Keep everything inside the pointed arch.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: The entrance procession in the order GIRM 120 gives it (thurifer; the cross between two lighted candles; other ministers; a reader with the Book of the Gospels, 'slightly elevated'; the priest last) while all stand for the Entrance Chant. The Sign of the Cross that follows at the chair (GIRM 124) is the card's excerpt, from the repo's Order of Mass.
